sentences.text: There was a dispute in respect of the performance of baby-shower.
Thereafter, on 16.07.2018 the respondent No.2 gave birth to a male child.
It is stated in the complaint that the delivery has taken place in the house of the respondent No.2.
After completion of four months, when she came to the matrimonial house, the petitioners quarreled with the respondent No.2 even for petty reasons, abused, assaulted her in one or other pretext.
It is further stated in the complaint that, the petitioners used to inform the parents of the respondent No.2 to take her back.
It is further stated in the complaint that the petitioner No.1 had illicit affair with one lady and there was quarrel in respect of the said incident.

In spite of repeated request made to the petitioner No.1 to stop the illegal relationship with that woman, he did not agree for the same and used to assault the respondent No.2 by stating that he would not leave that woman at any cost.
In the meantime, the respondent No.2 again became pregnant.

When she was carrying 03 months of pregnancy, the petitioners forced her to abort the said baby and also insisted her that, if she intends to deliver the baby, that baby should be given to her sister- in-law, as the sister-in-law did not have any child.

Such being the fact, on 16.11.2020 at about 09.30 p.m., when the respondent No.2 insisted the petitioner No.1 to stop the illegal relationship with that woman, the petitioner No.1 assaulted the respondent No.2 and threatened her with dire consequences.
It is stated in the complaint that the petitioners No.2
and 3 assaulted the respondent No.2 and supported the petitioner No.1

. As such,
consulting with elders and well wishers, the respondent No.2 lodged the complaint on 20.11.2020 belatedly.

The police have registered the case in Crime No.118/2020 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.
03.
Sri. Sanjeevkumar C. Patil, the learned counsel for the petitioners submits that there is omnibus allegations made out against the petitioners.
There is no overt-acts attributed against each individual.

The complaint came to be lodged on account of taking revenge against the husband and in-laws of the respondent No.2 with respect of illicit relationship stated to have had by the petitioner No.1 with other woman.
It is further submitted that the respondent No.2 had not mentioned the name of the woman with which the petitioner No.1 had illicit affair.
Mere, stating that, the petitioner No.1 had having illicit relationship with other woman, is not sufficient to infer the provision under Section 497 of IPC.
Making such submissions, the learned counsel for the petitioners prays to allow the petition and to quash the criminal proceedings against the petitioners.

04. Per contra, Sri. Shivashankar H. Manur, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - complainant vehemently opposed the petition and submits that the allegations are crystal clear against all the accused persons.
The respondent No.2 was assaulted and abused by one or other pretext.

When she went for postnatal rest to her parents' house, in the meantime the petitioner No.1 had relationship with another lady, for which there is frequently quarrel between the petitioners and respondent No.2.

The petitioners No.2 and 3 is being the parents of the petitioner No.1 have supported the act of the petitioner No.1 and used to abuse the respondent No.2, sometimes they have gone to the extent of assaulting the complainant on one or other pretext and asked her to get out from the house.
Such being the fact, it is not appropriate at this stage to scuttle the criminal proceedings at the initial stage.
Hence, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - complainant prays to reject the petition.

sentences.text: 3 05. The learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 - State submitted in support of submissions of learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - complainant and prays to reject the petition.

06. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and on perusal of the averments of the charge sheet and the complaint, it appears that On perusal of the records, it appears that on 16.11.2020 there was quarrel between the complainant and the petitioner No.1 in respect of alleged illegal affair that the petitioner No.1 had with another woman.

It appears from the records, the entire dispute revolving around the petitioner No.1 and the respondent No.2.
07.
No doubt, it is true that the inherent jurisdiction of this Court can be exercised sparingly with caution.

Further, it is guiding us that on plain reading of the averments of the complaint in its entirety, if it does not disclose prima-facie against the petitioners, the inherent jurisdiction can be exercise to avoid abuse of process of law.

08. Admittedly, in this case, on careful reading of the entire allegations on 16.11.2020 at about 09.30 a.m. when the respondent No.2 was insisting to forego the illegal relationship of the petitioner No.1 with another woman, there was a quarrel being ensued, at that time the petitioners No.2 and 3 have interfered and assaulted the respondent No.2.
Except this allegation, there are no other allegations made out against the petitioners No.2 and 3.
Even assuming that if this petitioners are subjected to face the trial, there would not be any possible conviction.
Therefore, in order to avoid the futile exercise it is necessary to scuttle the proceedings at the initial stage to secure the ends of justice.

09. In the light of above observations, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER I.
The petition is allowed in part.

II. The criminal proceedings against the petitioners No.2 and 3 in C.C.No.5995/2021 (Arising out of Vijayapur Women Police Station in Crime No.118/2020) for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC, is hereby quashed.
III. The liberty is reserved to the Trial Court to proceed against the petitioner No.1 in accordance with law.
In view of disposal of main petition, the pending I.A.No.1/2022 does not survive for consideration and hence the same is disposed of.
